tasks.short: Enter specified commands and test the final layout

steps.what: Interpret engineering specifications and approve exact commands, parameters and the target layout revision
Enter the specified commands and parameters into a working copy of the computer layout
Test final layout functions against specifications and accept or reject the changed working copy

tasks.design: Configure a parameterised native macro in the electrical design application in {OTHER}, using exact commands chosen from the specifications in {DOCS}. It changes a working copy only after the drafter's approval, and the drafter tests the resulting functions before accepting the layout.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated command entry can introduce transcription errors after the desired change is already specified.
tasks.enabler_now: Native macros can replay explicit, checked command sequences without interpreting design intent.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding what the command must accomplish and detecting unintended layout changes.
tasks.human_edge: The drafter can distinguish a command that ran successfully from a layout that meets the specification.
tasks.altitude: Less command transcription; change interpretation and test acceptance remain human.

reach.task: Explain a tested layout change and its limits
reach.learn: Parameter traceability and functional test evidence

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native macros can enter specified commands into a layout copy; the digest does not measure this task or establish functional correctness.

assumptions: Boundary is specified layout command entry and testing, not new circuit design or engineering release.

OTHER means the electrical design application. In s1 the drafter produces command names, order, parameter values, units, object IDs, application version, target layout revision and expected effects. Capture, interpretation and approval remain fully counted.
Only supported commands with explicit parameters can run. Missing values, changed target versions or unsupported functions stop the macro and use manual entry followed by s3 testing.
Test native macros first. Added macro-library maintenance is charged to other_role, while focal exception and change checks are charged below. Existing command runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Which commands repeat and are supported natively
Whether command entry is already automated
research_questions: Can a controlled replay remove transcription while preserving the same functional and unintended-change tests?

already_counted.description: Specify and approve commands, then test and accept the layout change

incremental.description: Resolve macro exceptions and verify changed parameter sets
Maintain supported macro sequences and version compatibility

approvals.approved_version: Exact ordered command list, parameters, application version and target layout revision approved in s1; any change voids approval
Exact changed layout snapshot and completed test findings accepted after testing; changes require retesting

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R80 gives gross20, less focal upkeep7 gives net13. Range0-3 assumes most commands are one-off or already automated and only a few supported repetitions change; test time is preserved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Copy printed circuit board fabrication drawings

steps.what: Select the correct fabrication drawings and set the print machine scale, media and copies
Collect and inspect copied drawings for revision, scale, legibility and completeness

tasks.design: Use the existing print or reproduction equipment in {OTHER} with controlled source files in {DOCS}. Retain source selection, physical handling and copy checks; machine print time is already equipment runtime.
tasks.previous_blocker: Remaining labour is choosing and checking a physical output, while reproduction itself is already mechanised.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software change is established for the remaining handling and inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting wrong revisions, distorted scale or reproduction defects.
tasks.human_edge: The drafter can inspect the actual copy that fabrication will use.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in copy preparation responsibility.

reach.task: Provide legible copies of the correct drawing revision
reach.learn: Reproduction scale and fabrication document controls

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: print machines already reproduce drawings; machine running time is not a new human labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes the drafter's setup, collection and inspection; printer runtime and fabrication work are excluded from the human baseline.

OTHER means print or blueprint reproduction equipment. The drafter selects source revision, scale, sheet size, media and copy count in s1; that capture time is fully counted. Missing revision or scale information requires manual clarification.
The print machine physically produces the copies consumed in s2 after s1 starts the job. Its runtime is not included in s1 or s2's human effort.
Keep existing native printing controls. No new workflow, integration or template is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: How much actual handling time remains today
research_questions: Is there avoidable duplicate printing that can be eliminated without shifting essential copy checking?

already_counted.description: Select, set up, handle and inspect physical drawing copies

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. Both a short print run and a run needing scale corrections retain full setup, handling and inspection time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select test-head drill size and submit the guide layout

steps.what: Select drill size from the test design and specifications and prepare the guide layout
outputs: proposed drill selection and guide layout

steps.what: Verify drill size and guide geometry, then submit the checked layout to the designated department
inputs: proposed drill selection and guide layout

tasks.design: Retain drill selection and guide checking in the fixture design application in {OTHER}, using specifications from {DOCS}. Native measurement tools support the drafter, while the submitted layout remains a checked human design choice.
tasks.previous_blocker: The correct tool depends on tolerances, fixture design and the actual specification.
tasks.enabler_now: No measured repetitive drafting component is established by this task or its digest.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting tolerances and ensuring the chosen hole and tool fit the test design.
tasks.human_edge: The drafter can recognise when a nominal drill size does not meet the intended fixture requirement.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in selection or layout submission authority.

reach.task: Explain the selected drill size and guide references
reach.learn: Fixture tolerances and tool selection constraints

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: test-head drill selection and guide verification depend on the actual design and tolerances; no saving is demonstrated by the digest.

assumptions: Boundary ends at guide submission; drilling and fixture manufacture remain outside and receive no claimed saving.

OTHER means the fixture design application. The drafter checks drawing revision, hole dimensions, tolerances, material, drill reference and guide geometry during s1 and s2. Capturing these facts is fully counted, with manual clarification for missing or contradictory values.
There is no assumed structured suitable-tool flag. The drafter makes and checks the selection against the source specification.
Use existing native drawing and measurement functions. No new tool or process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Which tolerances and tool constraints govern the fixture
Whether repeated guide detailing is significant
research_questions: Is there a repeatable guide-rendering substep distinct from drill selection and checking?

already_counted.description: Select and verify the drill and guide, then submit the layout

approvals.approved_version: Exact guide layout revision, drill reference and checked specification revision before submission; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. Standard and unusual drill sizes both retain full selection and layout checking time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plot test points and draw fixture wiring schematics

steps.what: Determine test points and fixture head connections, resolving layout coordinates and wiring references
outputs: checked test point and connection specification

steps.what: Plot the specified electrical test points and render the fixture wiring schematic
inputs: checked test point and connection specification

steps.what: Check plotted coordinates and schematic connections against the test intent before submitting the fixture drawings
inputs: checked test point and connection specification

tasks.design: Configure native coordinate import and schematic rendering in the fixture design application in {OTHER}. The drafter supplies the checked test-point and endpoint specification, then verifies coordinates, orientation and connection meaning against the source requirements in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordinates and connection references can be plotted repeatedly after the design is decided.
tasks.enabler_now: Native import and drawing templates can reproduce explicit coordinates and endpoint pairs.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing valid test points and recognising an incorrect coordinate frame or connection interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The drafter relates the drawing to the physical fixture and intended electrical test.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated plotting; test intent and drawing acceptance remain human.

reach.task: Provide a traceable fixture schematic for checking
reach.learn: Test point identification and coordinate-frame conventions

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: coordinate import and schematic templates can render explicit fixture data; the digest does not demonstrate autonomous test-point selection.

assumptions: Boundary covers fixture test-point plotting and wiring drawings, excluding test design, guide drill selection and physical fixture construction.

OTHER means the fixture design application. In s1 the drafter produces point IDs, coordinates, units, origin, orientation, head and frame pin references, endpoint pairs and source revision. Capture and resolving ambiguous mappings remain fully counted.

A fixture standards owner supplies the template and field mapping; added upkeep is counted as other-role work. Missing endpoints, unknown orientation or duplicate point IDs stop rendering and use manual plotting and checking in s3.
Test native import before custom code. The system cannot infer test coverage or suitability; existing rendering runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Whether plotting is already driven by structured fixture data
Which coordinate and pin-reference conventions apply
research_questions: Can native rendering remove plotting time without increasing mirrored coordinates or incorrect endpoint pairs?

already_counted.description: Specify points and connections and check the fixture drawing meaning

incremental.description: Handle import exceptions and verify mapping changes
Maintain fixture templates and import conventions

approvals.approved_version: Exact fixture sheet revision, coordinate frame, point list and connection specification checked before submission; changes require rechecking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R75 gives gross25, less focal upkeep8 gives net17. Range0-4 assumes only a minority of fixtures have repeated manual plotting and all point selection and meaning checks remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use native replay and rendering for specified repetitions while retaining layout tests, tool selection and physical copy checks.
reach: Explain fixture drawing references to test engineers
Provide fabrication staff with verified copies and guide layouts
role.ambitious_version: A drafter who can reproduce specified fixture and layout changes consistently while retaining full control over their technical meaning.
